title: GNNavigator: Towards Adaptive Training of Graph Neural Networks via Automatic Guideline Exploration
problem: Balancing GNN training runtime cost, memory consumption, and accuracy across diverse applications requires non-trivial optimization. Previous training methodologies suffer from inferior adaptability and lack a unified optimization solution.
motivation: Adaptive GNN training optimization enables efficient deployment across diverse applications with varying computational and memory constraints.
method: GNNavigator creates a unified description of both the software—the graph neural network training algorithm—and the hardware it runs on, so it can predict how they interact. It builds a model that forecasts the training's runtime and memory requirements. Then it automatically searches through different training configurations to find the combination that best balances execution speed, memory use, and accuracy for your specific task.
key_novelty: It treats software and hardware as a unified system, then automatically searches for the best training configuration of graph neural networks for each task.
contributions: Software-hardware co-abstraction framework for unified GNN training characterization
Performance model for predicting GNN training runtime and memory consumption
Automated design space exploration solution for configuration optimization
Achieves 3.1× speedup and 44.9% peak memory reduction with comparable accuracy
